articles.title: Martin Shkreli Caught Trading Pharma Stocks Despite Lifetime Federal Ban — FTC and 7 States Move for Contempt
articles.summary: The FTC and seven state attorneys general allege that 'Pharma Bro' Martin Shkreli violated his court-ordered lifetime ban on pharmaceutical industry participation by trading stocks in at least 60 drug companies. Federal authorities are seeking contempt sanctions and forfeiture of all trading profits. The case exposes how even judicially mandated pharma industry exclusions are treated as suggestions by those with enough capital and audacity.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Hid Safety Failures on iLet Diabetes Device — Stock Cratered 37% When Truth Emerged
articles.summary: A securities fraud class action alleges that Beta Bionics systematically misled investors about the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet insulin delivery device. When the concealed safety problems became public, shares collapsed over 37%. This is a textbook case of buried medical device safety data endangering patients while executives protected their stock positions.

articles.title: Ensign Group Accused of Hiding Patient Neglect, Falsifying Staffing Data, and Billing Fraud — Securities Fraud Suit Filed
articles.summary: Ensign Group, a major nursing facility operator, faces a securities fraud lawsuit alleging it concealed systematic patient neglect, understaffing, manipulated quality metrics, improper billing, and an administrator-license rental scheme. Investors were kept in the dark while vulnerable patients paid the price. The lawsuit reveals how corporate healthcare providers weaponize data manipulation against both regulators and the public.

articles.title: Forced Psychiatric Treatment and the Right to Refuse: The State's Growing Appetite to Medicate Against Your Will
articles.summary: A Reason analysis confronts the expanding legal and institutional framework allowing governments to compel psychiatric treatment on individuals diagnosed with mental illness, stripping them of informed consent rights. The piece names the core civil liberties conflict: if a diagnosis can override bodily autonomy, no one is truly safe from state-mandated medication. This is the quiet machinery behind psychiatric overreach that mainstream medicine refuses to interrogate.

articles.title: Estrogen Dominance, Histamine, and Endotoxin: The Metabolic Framework Mainstream Medicine Keeps Burying
articles.summary: Georgi Dinkov lays out a systems-level metabolic model connecting estrogen dominance, histamine excess, serotonin dysregulation, and endotoxin load — a framework with profound implications for fertility, energy metabolism, and chronic disease that institutional medicine ignores in favor of pharmaceutical symptom management. Blood estrogen levels routinely mislead clinicians while tissue-level estrogen excess drives pathology undetected. This is the kind of mechanistic synthesis that gets researchers defunded, not debated.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Securities Fraud Suit After FTC Complaint — Telehealth's Compounding Drug Profits Under Federal Scrutiny
articles.summary: Hims & Hers Health and its executives now face a securities class action lawsuit triggered by a sweeping FTC federal complaint alleging deceptive practices. The case puts a spotlight on the telehealth industry's aggressive commercialization of compounded drugs and raises questions about what executives knew and when they misled investors about regulatory risk. The FTC's intervention signals the federal government is finally examining whether direct-to-consumer pharma models prioritize profit over patient safety.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer's Continuous Genetic Evolution Exposes Why Standard Treatment Keeps Failing — And Why Oncology Won't Change Its Model
articles.summary: A landmark analysis of nearly half a million cells from dozens of pancreatic cancer patients reveals that tumor cells continuously reshape their genetic identity over time, systematically outmaneuvering static treatment protocols. The research exposes a fundamental flaw in the oncology establishment's one-time-biopsy, fixed-target treatment paradigm that has kept pancreatic cancer survival rates near zero for decades. The question that won't be asked in press releases: how much of this was knowable sooner, and what institutional incentives delayed the reckoning?

articles.title: Live Vaccines Given by Accident to 220 Immunocompromised IBD Patients — Zero Disease Cases, Zero Acknowledgment of What This Means
articles.summary: A study of 220 inflammatory bowel disease patients on immunosuppressive biologics who accidentally received live vaccines — including MMR and varicella — showed zero resulting cases of measles, mumps, or chickenpox. The findings directly challenge the blanket clinical dogma prohibiting live vaccines in immunocompromised populations, a restriction that has left millions inadequately protected. The medical establishment's silence on the natural immunity and vaccine safety implications of this data is deafening.

articles.title: FTC Moves to Hold 'Pharma Bro' Shkreli in Contempt — Caught Trading 60+ Drug Stocks Despite Lifetime Ban

This is what happens when the pharma ecosystem's worst actors face no real deterrence — they simply keep playing.

This is the psychiatric-state apparatus in action — and dissenting clinicians are being silenced.

articles.title: Estrogen, Serotonin, and Endotoxin: The Metabolic Framework Big Pharma Doesn't Want Taught in Med School
articles.summary: Researcher Georgi Dinkov breaks down how estrogen dominance, histamine dysregulation, serotonin excess, and endotoxin load interact to drive chronic disease — a framework rooted in the suppressed work of biologist Ray Peat. These mechanisms are routinely ignored in clinical training because they implicate dietary choices, endocrine disruptors, and gut dysfunction rather than patentable drugs. The implications for women's health, fertility, and metabolic disease are enormous.

articles.title: Placental GDF15 Deficiency Drives Fetal Growth Restriction — A Pregnancy Suppression Signal the System Has Barely Discussed
articles.summary: New research in PLOS Biology demonstrates that placenta-specific GDF15 is essential for fetal growth, with deficiency causing restriction through disruption of the fetal hepatic STAT3-IGF2 axis. Clinical studies have already linked low GDF15 levels to fetal growth restriction in humans, yet this mechanistic pathway has received virtually no mainstream clinical attention. At a time when miscarriage and fetal growth data are politically charged, this metabolic pregnancy research deserves far more scrutiny.
